Synopsis:
The AfD won ~44% in Saxony-Anhalt state elections, falling short of an outright majority (39/83 seats). Chancellor Merz reaffirmed the "firewall" against coalition with AfD but acknowledged a seismic shift in German politics. AfD is courting individual CDU lawmakers to form a state government — which would be a postwar first. The result signals deep unpopularity of Merz's coalition, rising Eurosceptic/pro-Russia sentiment in eastern Germany, and a broader European far-right momentum. Near-term risks include further state elections and potential erosion of the CDU firewall. Longer-term, the AfD is targeting 40%+ in the 2029 federal election, raising structural political risk for Germany's governance, EU cohesion, Ukraine support, and energy policy.
